correctness.rationale: An independent scalar harmonic calculation uses u=x+y/alpha−1−1/alpha and u'=1−y. Order-two harmonics and order-three solvability give a stable nondegenerate branch on alpha>alpha_H. If e is the u harmonic amplitude and q=gamma−1, then alpha−alpha_H=(gamma/(8q))e²+o(e²) and r²=gamma e²+o(e²). The order-three cosine forcing after subtracting the actual linear frequency gives C=(2q+1+2/q)/48. The square identity proves positivity and the unique minimum 5/48 at gamma=2. A differentiated tensor replay also reproduces the complex cubic coefficient; neither argument relies on finite-offset integration.
residual_risks: The optional recorded numerical table names DOP853, whereas the supplied solve_ivp call does not select it. Those numbers are illustrative, not a verification requirement. The result is local at fixed gamma, not uniform in gamma or a finite-amplitude bound.

value.rationale: A radial Hopf computation does not tell whether nonlinear oscillations run slower than the equilibrium's linear oscillatory mode at the same parameter. The substrate harmonic and physical time make this comparison operational. An exact positive correction over all real exponents and a unique minimizing exponent distinguish the nonlinear dynamical effect from the linear frequency drift, not just from another amplitude convention.
residual_risks: Sensitivity is relative to the chosen clock and substrate observable; the theorem neither endorses parameter fitting from large-amplitude data nor claims an invariant of every normal form.
